principleChecks.rationale: The theory precedes the example and names identification and division. The two numbered displays correspond to those source procedure steps, so numbering alone does not justify removal. However, neither solution display begins with an equals sign. The arithmetic is simple, the completed answer appears once, and there is no ambiguous repeated numeral within the given expression.

principlesChecked: One critical feature per example transition

principlesChecked: Different surface features and comparable initial demand
principleChecks.rationale: The first part changes the constant and supplied outside factor from the left example and requires new quotients; repeating the coefficient -8 across separate tasks creates no referential ambiguity. All retain the same extraction procedure; the supplied worked solutions explicitly show division, including the higher-power extension. Six guided parts do not violate the approximate seven-repetition preference.
